Automated Model Briefing

⚠ AI-generated text — may be wrong, incomplete, or overconfident. This is automated commentary on experimental model output, not flight advice and not a weather forecast. It has not been reviewed by a meteorologist.

Overall Assessment — Saturday is a cold, stable day with weak or no thermals at most sites. The model's thermal strength (w*) is near zero almost everywhere, which matches NWS Reno's soaring forecast: its trigger temperature of 49 degrees Fahrenheit (°F) is well above the expected high of 39 °F, and it forecasts a soaring index of 237 feet per minute (ft/min). Thin high cloud covers the sky from about 10am and dims the sun, and southwest wind across the Sierra crest builds through the afternoon, so Daydreams ridge soaring around midday is the best option; the model matched this morning's light winds at the valley airports to within about 2 miles per hour (mph), and the previous run showed stronger peak wind at Daydreams (20 mph, now 14 mph).

McClellan Marginal — Light wind lines up with the launch, but there are no thermals, so this is a sled ride only, with wind shear above launch.
Window: 9am–11am
w* is 0 ft/min. Launch wind is 4 mph from 139–146°, inside the preferred range, but the air is stable and most of the slope below launch is blocked, so ridge lift will be much weaker than the +66 to +75 ft/min shown. Wind shear peaks at 9 mph per 100 m at 727 ft AGL (caution). Wind 3,000 ft above ground is 15–18 mph and rises to 28 mph by 3pm.
West McClellan Marginal — There is a short ridge-lift window, but wind is often too southerly and strong wind sits just above launch.
Window: 10am–11am
There are no thermals (w* 0 ft/min). At 10am launch wind is 9 mph from 238° and ridge lift is +313 ft/min. By 11am wind has turned to 222°, crossing the launch, and ridge lift drops to +221 ft/min. Wind is 16–22 mph at 1,000 ft above launch in this window, and shear reaches 8 mph per 100 m at 558 ft AGL (caution). Launch temperature is 18–34 °F.
Daydreams Marginal — Ridge lift works at midday, but the wind is somewhat west of the southwest launch, thermals are weak, and wave risk grows after 1pm.
Window: 11am–2pm
w* is 156–165 ft/min, with a thermal top of 1346–1820 ft AGL. Launch wind is 11–13 mph from 256–270°, west of the 195–255° preferred range. Ridge lift is +231 to +279 ft/min, enough to soar. Shear reaches 8 mph per 100 m at 1,621 ft AGL (caution). At 8am cloud sits 500 ft above launch with cloud base (LCL) at launch height, so expect low cloud or fog early. Launch temperature is 29–33 °F.
Kingsbury grade Unfavorable — West-southwest wind blows over the back of this southeast-facing launch all day, with no thermals.
Peak thermal strength (w*) is 0 ft/min, and the thermal top (PBLH) reaches only 1483 feet above ground (AGL). Wind is 18–19 mph from 259–261° in the morning and 10–12 mph from 247–259° in the afternoon, never close to the preferred 104°. Ridge lift is near zero or negative (-98 to +47 ft/min).
Hallelujah Unfavorable — Wind on the west/southwest launch comes from the north in the morning and from the south in the afternoon, and lift is too weak to stay up.
Peak w* is 63 ft/min at 11am, with a thermal top of only 376 ft AGL. Afternoon wind is 1–12 mph from 151–181°, outside the 225–315° range; the 4pm ridge-lift reading of +176 ft/min comes from 175° wind, which crosses this launch. Launch is at or below freezing (24–36 °F).
Slide Mountain Unfavorable — Strong west-southwest wind puts the south/southeast launch on the downwind (lee) side, in heavy sink.
w* is 0 ft/min. Launch wind is 18–25 mph (peak 10 m wind 27 mph) from 229–259°, and 30–44 mph at 1,000 ft above launch from 11am. Air on the launch face sinks at -563 to -810 ft/min. Launch is 25–30 °F.
Peavine Mountain Unfavorable — Strong, rising southwest wind with sink on the launch face.
Peak w* is 9 ft/min. Launch wind is 14–18 mph in the morning and climbs to 26–32 mph from 1pm, from 215–238°. Wind at 1,000 ft above launch reaches 39–44 mph in the afternoon, and ridge lift is negative all day (-88 to -177 ft/min). Launch is 24–28 °F.
Rainbow Ridge Unfavorable — Too little lift to soar the east/northeast face, and the afternoon brings crossing wind and hazardous shear.
Peak w* is 73 ft/min at 11am, with a thermal top under 1000 ft AGL. Wind lines up with the launch only from 11am to 1pm, at just 2–4 mph, and ridge lift is +26 to +59 ft/min, far below the roughly 200 ft/min a glider sinks. From 2pm wind blows 7 mph from 192–205° (peak 13 mph at 3pm). Shear reaches 10 mph per 100 m at 565 ft AGL, which is the hazardous level.
Duck Hill Unfavorable — Wind blows from the southeast or south, behind the west-to-north launch, until the last hour, and lift is too weak even then.
w* is 0 ft/min. Wind is 4–6 mph from 131–193° until 4pm, when it turns to 279° at 4 mph with only +85 ft/min ridge lift, and evening flying ends at sunset. Shear reaches 9 mph per 100 m at 563 ft AGL (caution). Launch is 22–37 °F.

Hazards

  • Mountain wave and lee rotor, mid to late afternoon: Wind across the Sierra crest builds from 24 knots from 237° at 1pm to 28 knots from 225° at 3pm and 29 knots from 218° at 4pm, strong enough for rotor and wave turbulence downwind of the Carson Range and Peavine. NWS Reno also expects southwest wind near 10,000 ft to reach 30 knots from 1pm Saturday, bringing low-level wind shear (LLWS) and mountain wave turbulence through Sunday morning.
  • Strong wind on the high ridges: Slide Mountain sees 18–27 mph and Peavine Mountain 26–32 mph after 1pm, with 30–44 mph at 1,000 ft above both launches in the afternoon.
  • Wind shear near launch height: Wind changes sharply with height at Rainbow Ridge (10 mph per 100 m, hazardous), McClellan and Duck Hill (9 mph per 100 m), and West McClellan and Daydreams (8 mph per 100 m). Expect sudden speed changes on launch and during the climb-out.
  • Morning low cloud and freezing fog: At 8am the model puts cloud 500 ft above the Daydreams launch. NWS Reno expects freezing fog at Truckee until about 8–9am Saturday and a low chance near Carson City and Minden.
  • Bitter cold: Launch temperatures are 18–39 °F, and most launches stay at or below freezing for part of the day. Watch for frozen or snowy launch surfaces and for cold hands and stiff gear.
